name: SkillMax+
summary: My platform for tracking work, study and practice.
problem: Work, study and practice need a shared record to make progress visible without exposing private notes.
implementation: I built SkillMax+ and deployed it on Google Cloud with an API. It keeps the private source data separate from an authorized viewer and the public learning report on my portfolio.
highlights: Owner access manages learning paths, logs, Buildmap, exercises, visibility and planning.
Authorized viewers get a detailed read-only view; write requests are rejected.
The public learning report exposes sanitized, aggregated data for candles, theory, exercises, milestones, public builds and lastUpdated.
Internal synchronization records GitHub commit activity and successful Vercel production deployments as evidence of practice.

name: Acquisition Gap Analyzer
summary: A website-analysis MVP that ranks acquisition gaps using observable evidence from public pages.
problem: SMEs need specific, traceable website improvements rather than an unexplained AI score.
implementation: Built the analysis dashboard, bounded crawl pipeline, deterministic scoring and evidence-backed findings.
highlights: Firecrawl maps a domain and selects up to eight representative pages.
Six weighted categories produce three priority findings.
Competitor evidence is kept separate from the readiness score.
Optional OpenRouter rewriting cannot change scores or evidence.

name: StayAI
summary: A conversational hotel-discovery app with saved stays and explicitly simulated reservations.
problem: Hotel search, saved choices and reservation planning are usually split across separate interfaces.
implementation: Connected the conversation and hotel-data services to the interface, authentication, bookmarks and reservation records.
highlights: OpenRouter handles the conversation; Xotelo supplies hotel and rate data.
Owner-only database policies protect bookmarks and reservations.
A fixed demo account uses Supabase Auth.
Reservations are demonstrations: no payment, inventory hold or hotel confirmation.

name: Insurance Triage System
summary: An n8n workflow for visual and textual insurance-claim assessment, triage and human review.
problem: Claim intake needs structured processing while sensitive personal data and consequential decisions require care.
implementation: Designed the webhook intake, sensitive-data separation, AI assessment, structured output and review routing in n8n.
highlights: Separates personal data into a Google Sheets vault before AI assessment.
Uses GPT-5-mini with Gemini 2.5 Flash as a fallback.
Parses structured JSON and routes low-confidence or high-urgency claims to human review.
Coordinates claim logging, Gmail notifications and portal status updates.
A separate error path logs failures and alerts engineers.

name: AI Calendar Assistant
summary: An n8n assistant that uses conversational tool calls for scheduling and email.
problem: Scheduling requires context, availability checks and coordinated follow-up across calendar and email tools.
implementation: Designed the agent workflow, calendar tools, conversation memory, model fallback and response post-processing.
highlights: Google Calendar tools search, create and update events.
Window-buffer memory retains conversational context.
A prompt-level identity-first rule requests email verification.
Google Sheets lookup and Gmail tools support contextual responses and confirmations.

name: AI Newsletter Engine
summary: A scheduled workflow that curates AI news and distributes a document or email summary.
problem: Turning a stream of AI news into a consistent, readable newsletter involves repetitive filtering and formatting.
implementation: Built the RSS aggregation, deduplication, model synthesis, document generation and delivery routing workflow.
highlights: Scheduled RSS intake merges feeds and removes duplicate items.
Gemini and GPT model nodes support content synthesis.
Google Docs and Drive prepare downloadable documents.
Gmail and MailerLite support separate delivery paths.

name: Security Audit Checker
summary: A web application that scans publicly accessible application assets for security findings.
problem: Potential secret exposure and weak application settings need structured evidence and prioritisation.
implementation: Built the scanner, classification utilities, audit endpoint and reporting dashboard.
highlights: Recursive crawling inspects HTML and JavaScript assets.
Pattern matching and entropy analysis flag possible secrets.
Findings use CWE classification and CVSS severity fields.
JSON and Markdown reports distinguish validated and unverified findings.

name: Custom Donation Alerts
summary: A private client project that turns donations on an unsupported donation website into OBS streaming alerts.
problem: The client needed OBS alerts for website donations that standard services such as Streamlabs and StreamYard did not support.
implementation: Built a custom connection between the donation flow and streaming alerts for the client’s OBS setup.
highlights: Connects donations from the client’s donation website to streaming alerts.
Supports the client’s OBS setup where standard donation integrations were unavailable.
Developed as private client work; no public demo or source-code access.

name: MediaGen Orchestrator
summary: A conceptual media-workflow demo that connects a creative brief to research, creation and review stages.
problem: AI media workflows need a coherent interface for intake, progress and human feedback.
implementation: Built the briefing interface, workflow views and review screens around an n8n orchestration example.
highlights: The brief form can submit to a configured n8n trigger.
The included workflow separates research, creative and review agents.
Dedicated screens cover planning and human-in-the-loop review.
Simulation paths support demonstrating the interface without a connected backend.

name: GitHub PR Changes Extractor
summary: A utility that turns a public GitHub pull request into a downloadable JSON changeset.
problem: Raw diff files can be cumbersome to pass into an AI-assisted code-review workflow.
implementation: Built the PR URL interface, server-side GitHub extraction route and JSON download flow.
highlights: Parses a pull-request URL into repository and PR identifiers.
Fetches changed-file information through the GitHub API.
Exports structured changes as JSON for further analysis.

name: Video-Audio Extractor
summary: A browser-based tool that extracts audio from a selected video using WebAssembly.
problem: A simple audio extraction should not require an ad-heavy conversion site or a media upload.
implementation: Built the file drop zone, FFmpeg loading, format selection, progress feedback and local download flow.
highlights: FFmpeg runs in the browser through WebAssembly.
MP3, WAV and AAC use explicit conversion arguments.
Progress events drive the conversion indicator.
The result is downloaded through a browser Blob URL.

name: AI Compliance Navigator
summary: A NotebookLM research environment for exploring the EU AI Act and GDPR against a curated source collection.
problem: Developers need a way to locate and compare regulatory source material during AI research.
implementation: Curated the knowledge base and example questions for a source-backed NotebookLM research environment.
highlights: The source collection includes EU AI Act and GDPR texts.
EDPB guidance covers automated decision-making.
Example queries explore risk categories and documentation requirements.
This is a research environment, not a custom compliance engine or legal advice.

name: GitHub Repo Explorer
summary: A utility for browsing a public GitHub repository tree and exporting its structure as JSON.
problem: Understanding an unfamiliar repository requires a clear overview of its files and nested folders.
implementation: Built the repository URL validation, recursive tree transformation, expandable browser and JSON export.
highlights: Resolves the default branch through the GitHub API.
Builds a nested tree from the recursive Git Trees response.
Counts descendant files and folders.
Exports the resulting structure as JSON.

name: gijshulsebos.com
summary: A multilingual portfolio bringing projects, demos and certificates together in one interactive website.
problem: A varied collection of projects and learning achievements needs a clear, accessible presentation with room for technical detail.
implementation: Built the responsive bento grid, project expansion animations, certificate carousel and library, language switching and PDF preview processing.
highlights: Position-aware project expansion rearranges nearby cards while keeping Tarvos as the central project.
English, Dutch and German project content follows the selected language.
A fixed-slot certificate carousel links to specific certificates in a searchable library.
A Python pipeline validates GitHub PDFs, deduplicates files and generates WebP previews and a manifest.
Keyboard interactions and reduced-motion support complement hover and touch controls.

name: Hermes Oracle
summary: A website gateway that gave Hermes agents a JSON task with instructions for joining Discord: an experiment with Moltbook on Discord.
problem: Give Hermes agents a defined task for joining a shared Discord environment.
implementation: Built a website gateway that publishes the joining instructions as a JSON task.
highlights: Instructions published as a JSON task.
A joining task for Hermes agents.
An experiment with Moltbook on Discord.
sources: Project description supplied by the owner

name: AI Integration Registry
summary: A structured registry of AI providers and services, documenting integrations, capabilities, prompts and practical notes.
problem: AI integration knowledge is scattered across provider documentation and individual workflows.
implementation: Organized providers by service with a consistent set of Markdown documents and reusable templates.
highlights: A provider/service directory structure.
Separate capabilities, integration, prompts and notes documents.
Reusable templates for consistent service documentation.

name: TechEvents
summary: Discover hackathons and AI meetups, online and in the Netherlands and Belgium.
problem: Community events are spread across many calendars and platforms.
implementation: Built a filterable event dashboard with Firestore storage, a public read-only viewer and private owner selections.
highlights: Filter by date, language, source and location.
Open registration at the organizer’s website.
Google Calendar links prefill the event name, available dates and location.
Private selections are protected by Google sign-in; visitors need no account.

name: GenReel
summary: A portfolio of my generated media: AI images, video, voice, programmatic animations and personal creations.
problem: Different media techniques produce separate outputs. I wanted one place to present the work and show how those techniques come together.
implementation: I built GenReel to collect and present my media creations, combining AI generation and editing with programmatic video and Blender. The featured video demonstrates a 3D elevator safety scene.
highlights: Image-to-video and image generation, including work with Seedance 2.5.
AI voice generation and AI-assisted editing.
Programmatic video generation and Blender workflows with MCP.
A web portfolio built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, published on Vercel.

name: FilePrint
summary: An experimental Obsidian plugin that turns nested tags into visual fingerprints and procedural sound. Related notes share elements of their pattern and sound.
problem: A tag hierarchy describes how notes relate, but that relationship is not immediately visible or audible when browsing a vault.
implementation: I built local visual and audio generators and integrated them into an Obsidian plugin, with a sidebar, embedded note blocks and an interactive website to try the generators.
highlights: Shared tag prefixes drive related visual and musical parameters; note metadata also shapes visual details.
Canvas renders the visuals and Web Audio generates sound on demand, without automatic playback.
Independent visual and audio blocks, with local PNG, video and WAV exports.
The plugin runs without accounts, API keys, telemetry or runtime network requests.
An MIT-licensed experimental release, installed manually rather than through the Community Plugins directory.
